purpose: Bound the recurring GSP high-memory producer activity from a reusable frame-1200 save state.

observations.recurring_block: After initialization, each relative frame 3-59 emits exactly 16 full-word writes into 0xFFF98670-0xFFF98760, with a stable set of pointer-like and control-like values.
observations.initialization: Relative frame 1 emits 570 writes and relative frame 2 emits 85 writes across the surrounding 0xFFF982F0-0xFFF98760 region.
observations.pointer_landmark: The only write outside the main block is one write at 0xFFFCFC00 from PC 0xFFF418A0.
observations.record_walk_call_site: The filtered PC 0xFFF45060 probe reports writes at 0xFFF98510/0xFFF98520 during initialization, but the runtime instruction trace decodes 0xFFF45060 as CALLR FFF45090, the indexed-record reader entry. These events are not promoted as payload writes.

interpretation: This is direct GSP-side high-memory write activity following a saved gameplay state. Runtime traces classify the dominant recurring writer family in the analogous frame-600 probe as stack save/restore traffic, while the 0xFFF45060 event is an indexed-record reader call site rather than a proven payload writer. The actual upstream producer remains unresolved. No word, pointer, or block is promoted to track, road, object, HUD, craft, weapon, or armor semantics.
